text:
alana_cs: Heads-up - Lumina Labs onboarding. Their CI (GitHub Actions) kicks off 120 parallel integration jobs that all call our SDK during test setup. They see short 429 bursts and failing CI jobs right after a push. Pattern: spiky failures for ~30s, then succeed. Any quick advice to share with their SRE/CI team?

devin_sre: Ask for request ids + headers, but sounds like token-minting fanout from CI. Are they minting ephemeral tokens per job?

alana_cs: Yes, their pipeline step fetches a short-lived JWT from their auth service in each job and then runs tests that hit /v1/embeddings. Logs (sanitized):
```
2024-09-10T14:12:10Z job=17 POST /v1/embeddings 200
2024-09-10T14:12:11Z job=18 POST /v1/embeddings 429 X-RateLimit-Remaining:0
2024-09-10T14:12:11Z job=19 POST /v1/embeddings 429 X-RateLimit-Remaining:0
```

hiro_engineer: CI parallelism is a common onboarding footgun. Quick mitigations: (1) Use a single mint step that publishes the token to the Actions workspace and reuse it across parallel jobs (e.g., write to $GITHUB_WORKSPACE/.redwood_token before matrix starts). (2) Add a tiny randomized backoff in each job before the first outbound request (0-500ms). (3) If they can't share workspace, use actions/cache to store a token with TTL or a short-lived artifact via actions/upload-artifact + download in matrix jobs.

devin_sre: Also recommend reducing matrix concurrency during initial onboarding runs (set matrix.strategy.max-parallel or limit jobs) while they ramp. For ephemeral tokens minted by an internal auth service, we advise a single-flight fetch pattern in the job bootstrap: try read token file, else acquire lock, mint, write atomically.

alana_cs: Can you paste a small GitHub Actions snippet I can send to them that shows a central mint + reuse pattern?

hiro_engineer: Send this example: 
```
# single-token job (runs once before matrix)
- name: Mint Redwood token
  run: |
    token=$(curl -sS -X POST "https://auth.internal/mint?scope=redwood:embed")
    echo "$token" > $GITHUB_WORKSPACE/.redwood_token
- name: Upload token artifact
  uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
  with:
    name: redwood-token
    path: $GITHUB_WORKSPACE/.redwood_token

# matrix jobs: download and reuse
- name: Download token artifact
  uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
  with:
    name: redwood-token
- name: Small randomized jitter
  run: |
    jitter=$((RANDOM % 500))
    sleep $(echo "scale=3; $jitter/1000" )
- name: Run tests
  run: |
    token=$(cat .redwood_token)
    export REDWOOD_TOKEN="$token"
    node test/setup-and-run.js
```

ci-bot: Note: actions/cache is eventually consistent; prefer upload/download-artifact for immediate reuse across parallel jobs.

devin_sre: If they can't change CI flow, server-side mitigations: temporary onboarding quota bump or short tolerance window for token minting bursts (ops-only). But CS should approve. Client-side is fastest.

alana_cs: Sent snippet to customer. They implemented the single-mint+artifact pattern and added a jitter; CI failures dropped to near zero. They asked for a blurb to add to their onboarding docs.

hiro_engineer: Blurb: "CI matrix jobs often cause ephemeral-token stampedes. Recommended pattern: mint a single ephemeral token once per pipeline and share it with parallel matrix jobs (upload/download-artifact or workspace file), add a small randomized jitter (0-500ms) before the first SDK call, or temporarily limit matrix concurrency during initial ramps. These practices serialize token minting and prevent transient 429s without server changes." :white_check_mark:

alana_cs: Customer marked mitigated. infra-bot: please open a follow-up to add CI patterns to onboarding playbook and track proactive email to new accounts that run CI-heavy integrations.

infra-bot: Ticket CS-12100 created: Add CI token reuse & matrix guidance to onboarding docs; add proactive nudge for CI-heavy customers.

alana_cs: Closing thread unless they re-open. Thanks everyone :rocket:
